in_hebrew.name: פָּלָלְדִיָה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: פָּלָלְדִיָה היא שְׁם נָשִׁים שֶׁמֵתוֹכוֹ חיבור פָּלָל, פַּל, וְדִיָה, כָּל אֶחָד בוֹדִידוֹ. פָּל, פַּל, פָּלָל, אוֹ פָּלָלִי, הוא שֵׁם הָעִבְרִי, שֶׁפְּרוּשׁוֹ 'לָל' פְּעַל הַהִתְנַגָּשׁ, 'פַּל' נֶצַח, וְ'א' (אַ') כְּפֶל, אוֹ 'לָל' 'פַּל' 'א' (אַ'). דִיָה, דִי, אוֹ דִיָה (דִי), פְּעַל אוֹ נֶצַח, פְּרוּשׁוֹ 'דָ' (ד) 'יָה' (יָ).

in_greek.name: Παλλάδια
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Παλλάδια συνδυάζεται από τα ελληνικά στοιχεία Πάλλος (Πάλλος, Παλλάδος) και Δία (Δία). Ο Πάλλος (Πάλλος, Παλλάδος) είναι ο θεός των κυνήγι και της θάλασσής. Δία (Δία), ο θεός των ουρανών, της αιθέριας θάλασσής και του φωτός. Η Παλλάδια συνδυάζεται επίσης με το όνομα της Παλλάς (Πάλλας), που σημαίνει «θύελλα» και συνδέεται με την Αθηνά.

in_latin.name: Palladia
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Palladia a partibus Pallus et Dia ductum est. Pallus, dei cuniculi et maris, et Dia, dei caeli, aetherei maris et lucis. Palladia etiam cum nomine Palladae, quae significat «tempestas», et conexio habet cum Minerva.

historical_references.reference: Palladia was a title given to a statue of Athena, worshipped in the city of Palladium in ancient Greece. The legend arose that the statue had been brought from Troy to the city of Pavia in Italy. Christians believed that the statue had the power to protect the city from destruction. When the city was besieged by Attila the Hun in 452 AD, the bishop of Pavia took the statue to Ravenna for safekeeping. When the Huns arrived, they found the city undefended but were unable to take it, and the city was spared. This event reinforced the belief in the power of the statue, and it became known as the 'Virgin of Victory'.

During the early Christian period, there were several shrines dedicated to the Virgin Mary, collectively known as the 'Holy Shrines of the Theotokos'. One of these shrines was located in the city of Palladia in Dalmatia. The city was named after a local saint named Palladia, who was said to have been a Christian martyr during the Diocletian persecutions. The shrine was an important pilgrimage site, and the Virgin Mary was believed to have appeared to Saint Palladia in a vision, promising to protect the city and its people.
